summary.headline: Raises the part of a home's value that school taxes skip from $100,000 to $140,000.
summary.plainEnglish: Texas homeowners pay school property taxes on their home's value minus a set amount. This bill raises that amount from $100,000 to $140,000 for a home the owner lives in, and the state pays school districts for the money they lose. It takes effect only if voters approve a matching change to the Texas Constitution; the Governor signed it on June 16, 2025.

howItWorksToday.text: School districts in Texas tax homes based on their value. A home the owner lives in gets a set amount taken off its value before the school tax is figured.
The amount was $15,000 until 2015, when voters approved $25,000. Voters approved $40,000 in May 2022 and later $100,000, the amount today.
Under current law, part of what school districts lose to this tax break is covered by the state.
The Texas Constitution sets this amount, so an increase also needs voters to approve a change to the constitution.

changes.label: The part of a home's value that school taxes do not count
changes.today: School districts do not tax the first $100,000 of the value of a home its owner lives in.
changes.ifPassed: School districts would not tax the first $140,000, starting with the 2025 tax year.

changes.label: Money for school districts that collect less
changes.today: The state gives school districts extra money to make up for the 2023 increase in this tax break.
changes.ifPassed: Beginning with the 2025-2026 school year, the state must also make up what districts lose from this increase.

changes.label: When the change starts
changes.today: The $100,000 amount stays in place unless voters approve a change to the Texas Constitution.
changes.ifPassed: The $140,000 amount takes effect on the day the voters' approval takes effect. If voters say no, it never takes effect.

changes.label: What the state would pay
changes.today: The state pays nothing for this increase, because it is not in effect.
changes.ifPassed: The state would pay about $1,324.2 million in the 2026 budget year and $1,418.4 million in 2027, the Legislative Budget Board estimates.

summary.whyNow: The Senate approved the final version 31 to 0 on May 29, 2025, after the House approved it 143 to 0. The Governor signed it on June 16, 2025; the larger tax break still depends on voters.
summary.question: Do you support raising the school tax break on a home from $100,000 to $140,000?

whatItDoes.text: Raises the amount of a home's value that school districts may not tax from $100,000 to $140,000, for a home the owner lives in.
Requires the state to give school districts extra money, beginning with the 2025-2026 school year, to make up for the taxes they no longer collect.
Takes effect only if voters approve a matching change to the Texas Constitution; otherwise the increase has no effect.

whoItAffects.text: Adults in Texas who own the home they live in: $40,000 more of the home's value would be free from school district taxes.
School districts, which would collect less in local property tax and receive state money in its place.

summary.whatChangesForYou: A couple who own and live in a house in Texas would have $140,000 of its value left out of their school tax bill, up from $100,000. The bill's author estimates this saves a homeowner $363.44 at the statewide average school tax rate.

caseFor.argument: The increase would save a homeowner an estimated $363.44 in school taxes at the statewide average rate, and the state would make up any funding school districts lose.
caseFor.attribution: the author's statement of intent in the Senate Research Center bill analysis

unknowns: The sources gathered do not show whether voters approved the change to the Texas Constitution.
